source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Rear Suspension and Drive Line, p.4-20

procedures.title: Rear strut rod and bracket: remove, repair and install
steps: (continued) ...over the strut shaft; fit washer and nut and torque to specification.
Lower the car to the floor, then torque the camber cam nut and the strut rod shaft nut to specification and fit the cotter pin through the rod bolt.
Check rear camber and adjust if needed.

procedures.title: Rear transverse spring: remove, repair and install
steps: Raise the rear and support it on the frame just ahead of the torque control arm pivots; remove the wheels and tires.
Put a floor jack under the spring at the link bolt and raise the spring until it is almost flat.
Wrap a 1/4" or 5/16" chain with grab hook around the suspension crossmember and spring and hook it tight; C-clamp the chain to the spring so it cannot slip (see figure 50 in the manual).
Lower the jack to unload the link bolt; remove the link bolt cotter pin, nut and rubber cushions.
Raise the spring end with the jack again as before and take off the chain once it goes slack.
Lower the jack slowly until spring tension is fully released.
Repeat these steps on the other side.
Remove the 4 bolts and washers holding the spring center clamp plate (see figure 51 in the manual).
Drop the spring and slide it out from under the car (see figure 52 in the manual).
notes: Caution: only use 1/4" or 5/16" chain with a safe grab hook to hold the spring; never rope, wire, cable or other means.
Figure 49 in the manual shows the spring mounting: link bolt, cushions, cushion retainers and plate.
